sentences.text:
THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR HEARING, THIS DAY,
JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE T.G. SHIVASHANKARE GOWDA  ORAL JUDGMENT
In this appeal, the petitioner is seeking enhancement of compensation.
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties shall be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal.

3. The undisputed facts is that, on 13.03.2014 at 06.30 p.m., there was an accident between motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-19/Q-2318 in which the petitioner was a pillion rider and a jeep bearing No.KA-32/MB- 1818, the petitioner suffered fracture to left Femur.
After taking treatment, the petitioner approached the Tribunal for grant of compensation under Section 163A of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ('the Act' for short).
Claim was opposed by the Insurance Company.

After taking the evidence and hearing both parties, the Tribunal by impugned judgment awarded compensation of NC: 2024:KHC:32702 Rs.12,256/- with 6% interest p.a., Pleading inadequacy and seeking enhancement of compensation, the petitioner is before this Court.

4. Heard the arguments of Sri.Rajaram Sooryambail, learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri.B.Pradeep, learned counsel for the Insurance Company.
5. It is contended by the learned counsel for the petitioner that medical evidence through PW-2 explains 25% of whole body disability suffered by the petitioner on account of fracture of left Femur.

No compensation was awarded towards loss of income during laid-up and the petitioner is not awarded with just compensation and sought for enhancement.
6.

Per contra, the learned Counsel for the Insurance Company has contended that the compensation awarded is proportionate to the injuries and the petitioner cannot claim compensation as it is a NC:
2024:KHC:32702 petition filed under Section 166 of the Act and he has supported the impugned judgment.

7. I have given my anxious consideration to the arguments addressed on behalf of both sides and Sunil vs Gopala Gowda on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/81635417/
2 also perused the materials on record.
8.
It is undisputed that the award of the Tribunal has been satisfied by the Insurance Company.
9. The medical records show that the petitioner has suffered fracture of left Femur.
The medical evidence through PW-2/Dr.Suresh Mankar shows assessment of 25% of whole body disability.
Having regard to the age of petitioner at 18 and he has just entered the age of earning, his notional income has to be taken at Rs.3,300/- per month and disability has to be assessed at 15%.
Loss of income during laid-up of three months has to be considered at Rs.9,900/- (Rs.3,300/-x3) and loss of disability will be: Rs.3,300/-x12x16x15% = Rs.95,040/-.
By default, the petitioner is entitled to pain and suffering of Rs.5,000/-; reimbursement of medical NC: 2024:KHC:32702 expenses at Rs.7,256/-.
Total compensation comes to Rs.1,07,296/- as against Rs.12,256/- assessed by the Tribunal, thereby enhancement of Rs.95,040/-.
It is the just compensation that the petitioner is entitled to, in the facts and circumstances of the case.
